advances: Conditional on the given marked normal-marginal law and its exact allocations. The orientations constrain a section body in dimension two. The triangle bound assumes homothetic caps, and the midpoint example calibrates aggregate area.

proof:
For each record and fiber the effective measure is the selected old normal measure plus the allocated section area placed at $-u/|u|$. A proper cut creates its cut face with precisely that outer normal. At an inside support the old face has normal $-u/|u|$ and the two fractions sum to one. At an outside support the old face has normal $u/|u|$ and the two equal allocated masses produce the two opposite atoms. Lower-dimensional touches have zero area and pure-base records reduce to their allocated whole-fiber choices. The complement reverses the continuous cap normal and uses the complementary body selector with the original section. Every such effective area measure and each full-body area measure has zero vector first moment, by constant-field divergence for positive-volume bodies and by cancellation for the paired atoms. Integration gives both asserted measures and $\int n\,dR(n)=0$. The integrals are finite even when $u$ approaches zero, since $|u|T_{H,z}$ is bounded by the maximal hyperplane section area of an enclosing ball.

For a planar body with support function $h(\vartheta)$, its area measure on the normal circle is the distribution $h''+h$, with a segment contributing its length at each of its opposite perpendicular normals and a point contributing zero. For polygons this follows by solving $h''+h=0$ between edge normals and taking the jumps of $h'$ at those normals. Polygonal approximation gives the general formula by uniform support-function convergence and weak continuity of ordinary area measure. One way to see the latter for positive bodies is to use radial graphs about a common interior ball: the convex gauges converge uniformly, their gradients converge almost everywhere by the subgradient inequalities, and the normal-weighted radial area elements are uniformly bounded. For a segment, the support is linear in the direction on each open semicircle separated by its perpendiculars, and the two derivative jumps are its length. Equality of area measures implies that the support functions differ by a first harmonic, which is a translation.

A nonnegative finite circle measure of zero vector first moment is represented by such a planar body. To see this, partition the circle into short arcs. Replace the mass on each arc by an atom in the direction of its vector integral, with mass equal to the length of that integral, omitting zero vectors. The arc diameters tend to zero, so these measures converge weakly to the given measure. Their vector moments remain zero and their total masses are bounded by the given mass. Rotate each atom vector counterclockwise by a right angle and concatenate the resulting edges in cyclic normal order. They form a closed convex polygonal curve. Indeed, starting with any edge normal, the scalar increments in that direction are nonpositive over the next half-circle and nonnegative over the other half-circle. Closure keeps the path in the supporting halfplane of the starting edge. Each edge thus belongs to the boundary of the convex hull of the path. In the collinear case the two equal opposite edges represent a segment, and the zero case is a point. Anchor these polygons at an initial vertex at the origin. Their diameters are uniformly bounded by their total edge lengths. A Hausdorff subsequential limit represents the desired measure by the support-function distribution formula. Apply this to $R$ to obtain $J$.

At a positive planar cap use its actual cap body as representative $D_{z,H}\subseteq K_z$. At an outside supporting facet use a subsegment of its face with length $m$. At a zero contribution use a point of $K_z$. Such choices are Borel. For positive caps their support functions are Borel by continuity in the plane parameters on the strictly proper stratum, with constant supports at full caps. At an outside support one can shorten the supporting segment about its midpoint. Its endpoints are Borel on this stratum, for example by taking the extrema of the tangential coordinate on the exposed face as limits of extrema over compact slices with positive thickness. At pure-base records choose the entire fiber or a fixed point according to the selector. All representatives lie in the same fixed bounded set. The support function
$$
h_A=\sum_z\int h_{D_{z,H}}\,d\theta
$$
is a finite continuous sublinear function, and $h_A\le h_B$ since $\theta$ is a probability law. Linearity of $h''+h$, including after integration against this law, gives $S_A=\beta S_B+S_J$, hence $A$ is a translate of $\beta B+J$. Subtracting $\beta h_B$ from $h_A\le h_B$ gives the first oriented inclusion. Apply the same argument to the complement, whose section measure is $R^-$ and whose section body is $-J$ up to translation. Taking difference bodies and areas gives the stated bounds.

Multiply each recordwise identity and each representative support function by $\lambda_z$ before summing the fibers. The tested normal-marginal equality applies to this weight, so the preceding argument gives the weighted statements with the same allocations. Convexity of the actual underlying set gives $B_\lambda\subseteq K_p$ at its integer mean. At bases $-1,0,1$, an affine weight with mean zero must have equal endpoint values, so it is constant and $J_\lambda$ is a translate of $J/3$.

For the triangle calibration, center the triangle $T$ at its centroid and normalize its three facet functionals $\ell_i$ by $h_T(\ell_i)=1$. They sum to zero, as is seen by evaluating their sum on the three vertices, where the opposite-facet value is $-2$. Thus $h_{-T}(\ell_i)=2$. The inclusion $-T+q\subseteq cT$ implies $2+\ell_i(q)\le c$ for each $i$, hence $c\ge2$, and $-T\subseteq2T$ by the same facet inequalities. If all caps are translates of $aT$ with area fraction $\beta=a^2$, their average cap body is a translate of $aT$. Consequently $J$ is a translate of $(a-\beta)T$ and the reflected inclusion gives $2(a-\beta)\le\beta$, or $\beta\ge4/9$. The three equally weighted centroid vertex caps have $a=2/3$ by barycentric coordinates. On each old edge, its two incident caps each cover a fraction $2/3$, so the marginal fraction is $4/9$ and $J$ is a translate of $(2/9)T$.

For the actual three-fiber midpoint calibration, $K_-+K_+\subseteq2K_0$ gives $B\subseteq3K_0$. Thus a translate of $-J$ lies in $3\beta K_0$ and $|J|\le9\min(\beta,1-\beta)^2|K_0|\le9\min(\beta,1-\beta)^2M$ where $M=\sum_z|K_z|$. The endpoint rectangles $[-R,R]\times[-1/R,1/R]$ and its coordinate swap have area four each. Their lifted convex hull has midpoint fiber the Minkowski average, a square of side $R+1/R$. For these fibers $B=3K_0$ and $|B|/M=9(R+1/R)^2/((R+1/R)^2+8)\to9$.
statement:
Let $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$, be positive-volume compact convex bodies at a finite set of bases. Let $\theta$ be a probability law of jointly measurable cap records $H=\{a\cdot z+u\cdot x\ge c\}$ and their allocated body selectors $s_H\in[0,1]$. On proper cuts use the captured old boundary and full section area. On inside supporting facets use body density $\alpha$ and section density $1-\alpha$, and on outside supporting facets use $\alpha$ for both. Strictly full and empty fibers have their usual selectors. At pure-base records allow complementary whole-fiber choices at equality and set section coarea to zero. On nonvertical records let $T_{H,z}$ be the allocated section area divided by $|u|$ and $T_H=\sum_z T_{H,z}$. Let $S_K$ denote the outer normal area measure of $K$, and suppose the mean selected old-boundary normal measure is $\beta\sum_z S_{K_z}$ with $0<\beta<1$. Set
$$
R=\int_{u\ne0}|u|T_H\,\delta_{-u/|u|}\,d\theta.
$$
An effective area measure is the ordinary measure for a positive-volume cap, zero for an empty cap or a touch of dimension below $d-1$, and $m(\delta_{u/|u|}+\delta_{-u/|u|})$ at an outside supporting facet with allocated area $m$. At a pure-base equality take the effective measure according to the allocated whole-fiber choice. The mean effective cap and complementary cap measures are, respectively,
$$
\beta\sum_z S_{K_z}+R,\qquad (1-\beta)\sum_z S_{K_z}+R^-,
$$
where $R^-$ is the reflection of $R$. The complement uses $1-s_H$ and the same allocated section. In particular $\int T_Hu\,d\theta=0$.

If $d=2$, put $B=\sum_z K_z$ (Minkowski sum). There is a compact convex $J$, possibly a point or segment, unique up to translation with $S_J=R$. There are translations $q,q'$ with
$$
J+q\subseteq(1-\beta)B,\qquad -J+q'\subseteq\beta B.
$$
In particular $J-J\subseteq\min(\beta,1-\beta)(B-B)$ and $|J|\le\min(\beta,1-\beta)^2|B|$.

Suppose in addition that the same law satisfies the selected old-boundary normal-marginal identity tested against $\omega(z)\phi(n)$ for every affine $\omega$ on the base and continuous normal test $\phi$. For a nonnegative affine weight $\omega$ on the finite base set with positive sum, put $\lambda_z=\omega(z)/\sum_y\omega(y)$, $B_\lambda=\sum_z\lambda_z K_z$ and
$$
R_\lambda=\int_{u\ne0}\sum_z\lambda_z|u|T_{H,z}\,\delta_{-u/|u|}\,d\theta.
$$
Then $R_\lambda=S_{J_\lambda}$ for a planar convex $J_\lambda$, and there are translations of $J_\lambda$ and $-J_\lambda$ inside $(1-\beta)B_\lambda$ and $\beta B_\lambda$, respectively. If $p=\sum_z\lambda_z z$ is integral and the bodies are the actual fibers of a convex set there, both containments hold with $K_p$ in place of $B_\lambda$.
title: Allocated cap area measures and an oriented planar section body
